evidence: app/react-router.config.ts:6 — only `ssr: true`; no future/unstable flags at all
app/app/routes.ts:1-9 — plain `index`/`route` config, no `unstable_*` route helpers or RSC config
app/package.json:12-25 — react-router 8.5.0 (current stable, released 2026-10-19 per reactrouter.com/changelog); vite ^8.0.3 (stable since 2026-03-12)
app/vite.config.ts:7 — `resolve.tsconfigPaths: true`, the single recently-stable API (Vite 8.0, `@experimental` marker removed 2026-07-22)
app/app/root.tsx:3-10 — Link/NavLink/Outlet/ScrollRestoration/Scripts/Meta/Links only; no view transitions (deprecated in 8.5.0), no react-router-dom (removed in v8)
reach.rationale: The entire React Router surface is long-stable, and the config enables zero future/unstable flags; the only recently-stable item is a one-line Vite 8 resolver option in the build config, so this sits between 'only long-stable' and 'recently-stable in central places'.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:7 — the only new-ish API, isolated in the build config, not imported anywhere in app code
app/app/lib/api.server.ts:1-88 — all server data access built on plain `fetch`, `data()` and module-scoped caching; no experimental data-loading APIs
app/app/components/ui.tsx:1-2 — only `useId`, `Link` and custom components; nothing framework-risky in shared components
containment.rationale: There is essentially nothing to contain: the single recently-stable option lives in one config line, and every route/component module sticks to APIs that have been stable for over a year.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:7 + app/tsconfig.json:14-16 — tsconfigPaths enables the `~/*` alias without the third-party vite-tsconfig-paths plugin, which Vite now warns against (vitejs/vite#21781)
app/app/root.tsx:27-49 — root `Layout` export keeps the shell across error states, the current recommended pattern (stable since 7.16)
app/app/routes/not-found.tsx:3-5 — 404 via thrown `data()` is the documented loader pattern
justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used at all, and the one recently-stable use is exactly the framework's recommended replacement for a community plugin, buying a dependency-free alias setup.

findings.issue: Uses Vite 8's `resolve.tsconfigPaths`, which only lost its `@experimental` documentation marker on 2026-07-22 and depends on the Rolldown resolver (occasional alias-resolution bugs have been reported in the new pipeline).
findings.suggestion: Keep it, but if alias resolution ever misbehaves after a Vite bump, fall back to an explicit `resolve.alias` entry for `~/*` — a one-line, low-risk swap.

summary: This is a deliberately conservative app: react-router 8.5.0 (the current stable release) with zero unstable/experimental/future-flag APIs, no RSC, no middleware, and no use of the APIs deprecated in 8.5.0 (view transitions, react-router-dom, meta `data`). The only new-ish item is Vite 8's recently-stable `resolve.tsconfigPaths` in a single config line, used exactly as Vite recommends. Risk of breaking-change fallout is minimal.
